## Reviso review — detached HEAD ce2dcc537b vs 85737f52b5 (1 commit, 8 files)
Base: 85737f52b59aa2e3403c9b8e48acf71ccc5bfae3 via flag — merge-base 85737f52b5

Found 3 issues:

1. [P1][conf 95] Remove old local recovery codes after creating federated replacements — server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:126
   Failure: Regenerating codes into user storage leaves an existing local set valid; credential validation still falls back to that old set.
   Fix: After successful user-storage creation, remove existing locally stored recovery-code credentials.
   (bugs)

2. [P2][conf 100] Consume recovery codes after successful validation — testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340
   Failure: The test provider accepts every generated code repeatedly and always presents the first code; exhaustion never triggers regeneration.
   Fix: Validate the next unused code and persist its consumption before returning success.
   (bugs)

3. [P2][conf 95] Preserve recovery credential IDs and support removal — testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:242
   Failure: Account REST receives a recovery credential with no ID, preventing removal; the provider also lacks recovery-code disabling.
   Fix: Copy the stored credential ID into the returned model and implement recovery-code disabling and its advertised disableable type.
   (bugs)

findings.title: Remove old local recovery codes after creating federated replacements
findings.failure_scenario: A federated user with locally stored recovery codes regenerates them after the storage provider gains recovery-code support. The new set is stored externally, but an old local code still authenticates through local validation fallback.
findings.suggested_fix: After updateCredential succeeds, remove the user's existing locally stored recovery-authn-codes credentials so regeneration invalidates the previous set.
findings.evidence: CredentialHelper.java:125-129 bypasses RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential, whose services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:39-42 removes the previous stored credential. model/storage/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/UserCredentialManager.java:66-78 still invokes local validators when external validation fails.

findings.title: Consume recovery codes after successful validation
findings.failure_scenario: After a successful recovery-code login through the test provider, the same code authenticates again indefinitely. Subsequent challenges still request the first code, and exhausting the set never triggers regeneration.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the next unused recovery code and persist its removal before returning true; retain code numbering and remaining-code state when returning the credential.
findings.evidence: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:334-340 checks membership without updating storedRecoveryKeys, while :237-241 reconstructs the full original set on every read. The local implementation in services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/credential/RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:118-119 explicitly removes and persists the consumed code.

findings.title: Preserve recovery credential IDs and support removal
findings.failure_scenario: A user requests recovery credentials through Account REST and receives a model with a null ID, so the credential cannot be addressed for deletion. Even deletion through the legacy type placeholder leaves the recovery codes configured because the provider only disables OTP.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the returned model's ID from myUser.recoveryCodes, clear recoveryCodes in disableCredentialType for this type, and include it in getDisableableCredentialTypesStream.
findings.evidence: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:195 assigns a stored ID, but :237-242 returns a freshly constructed model without copying it; :215-222 only implements OTP disabling. services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/requiredactions/util/CredentialDeleteHelper.java:64-69 resolves federated credentials by ID and then invokes disableCredentialType.
